A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRWM research. All 17 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v3, including appendices, were readable. Retitling, reorganization and identifiable content omissions do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original rollout experiments, latent probing and clustering, and component ablations across three deterministic environments.

after.justification: v3 retains original rollout and representation results and adds Maze 9x9 perceptual metrics and Atari experiments in supplementary Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: The CNN plus causal Transformer encoder, instantaneous decoder, normalized projection head, all-pairs slowness loss, uniformity loss and combined reconstruction/KL objective are unchanged. The expanded oracle description documents the existing diagnostic experiment; the Atari results do not establish a method adaptation.

E1.justification: Supplement C in v3 adds evaluated Atari environments Asterix and Breakout, extending coverage from static 3D navigation environments to dynamic game settings. The original two maze datasets and Minecraft environment remain. The Atari extension is explicitly limited to two games.

E2.justification: The main Standard Diffusion, Video Diffusion, Diffusion Forcing and oracle comparisons remain. However, the supplementary comparisons against Adjacent-Only regularization, no-projection and single-loss variants disappear with v1's detailed ablations. No new external comparison method is demonstrated.

E3.justification: v3 adds SSIM and rFID evaluation on Maze 9x9 and PSNR/SSIM evaluation for Atari. The retained frame-wise MSE comparisons, rollout horizons and held-out MLP probing procedure are unchanged. The added evaluations are sparsely specified; no change to retained training budgets or rerunning of existing experiments is established.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix B reports loss-term removal, projection-head removal, latent dimensions 16/32/64/128, and all-pairs versus adjacent-only regularization studies. Their tables, curves and detailed findings are absent from v3. Section 7 and Supplement E merely list these studies and refer to supplementary results. Latent probing, clustering and rollout case studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both mention a fixed seed for maze-map generation, rather than seed-based uncertainty estimation. The added tables likewise report single estimates.

E6.justification: Figure 3's rollout curves and Table 1's probing scores are unchanged. v3 adds perceptual and Atari results: for example, its Table 2 reports DF rFID of 4.4345 for the baseline versus 2.8729 with regularization, and Table 3 reports Breakout PSNR of 34.23 versus 37.76. v1's detailed ablation results disappear. These are added and removed results, not same-setting improvements between versions.

T1.justification: The deterministic formulation and mathematical definitions of the representation and losses remain unchanged. Neither version develops formal guarantees or proofs. v3's additional oracle equations explain an existing implementation rather than introduce new theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central representation-bottleneck claim remains. v3 narrows the novelty framing from a 'novel geometric regularization loss' to applying established temporal contrastive principles, explicitly emphasizes controlled diagnosis, and no longer lists state-of-the-art performance as a main contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limitations concerning environment complexity, visual artifacts, temporal-Transformer overhead and a still-large oracle gap. This qualifies v1's minimal-overhead discussion and more general residual-misalignment caveat. Conversely, explanations tied to the removed ablations, including projection/reconstruction decoupling and adjacent-only shortcuts, disappear.

D1.justification: v3 removes v1's training Table 4, including optimizer schedules, regularization weights, architecture settings and sampling parameters, and substitutes a repository link for the earlier promised release. It adds oracle implementation and image-normalization details. Minecraft documentation now specifies recorded state trajectories rendered with Blender, whereas v1 specified Malmo collection; this does not establish that the dataset or experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v3 adds a substantial Related Work section and many references covering video-world-model architectures, latent representations and temporal contrastive learning. It explicitly positions GRWM as using established contrastive principles to regularize a world-model autoencoder, expanding and refining v1's shorter positioning around trajectory regularization.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution list and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related Work, Representation as the Bottleneck and Limitations become separate sections, the oracle explanation expands, and the appendices are reordered. This substantially changes the narrative despite retaining much of the method and experimental text.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column layout to two columns, substantially resizing and relocating figures. v1's ablation plots/tables and training table disappear, while two new supplementary result tables appear. Retained trajectory/environment figures are relocated and renumbered; clustering panels lose their axes, with normalization explained in the caption.

improvement.justification: v3 improves positioning, oracle explanation and limitations, and adds perceptual metrics and limited dynamic-environment validation. However, it removes the detailed component ablations and in-PDF training configuration, weakening support for design choices and reproducibility while retaining references to missing ablation results. The linked repository's contents are not established by the PDFs. These material gains and losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
